title: Late Breaking Results: Breaking Symmetry - Unconventional Placement of Analog Circuits using Multi-Level Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
problem: Analog circuit performance is severely impacted by layout-dependent effects (LDEs); conventional symmetric placement mitigates variations but is suboptimal due to non-linear nature of LDEs, leaving performance on the table.
motivation: Traditional symmetric analog layout design is conservative; exploring asymmetric placements guided by learning can exploit non-linear LDE physics to improve performance and robustness.
method: Proposes multi-level, multi-agent Q-learning framework for objective-driven analog layout optimization. Agents explore unconventional (asymmetric) placement strategies in design space using reinforcement learning. Approach is guided by functional and timing simulations to validate performance improvements. Comparison with simulated annealing baseline demonstrates RL superiority.
key_novelty: First application of multi-agent reinforcement learning to analog layout automation, breaking conventional symmetry constraints to optimize performance.
contributions: Multi-agent RL framework for analog circuit placement
Better variation performance than state-of-the-art symmetric layout techniques
Demonstrates RL superiority over simulated annealing

metrics.other: Variation performance improvement vs. symmetric layouts

limitations: Evaluation on specific analog circuits; generalization to different circuit topologies and technology nodes not discussed.
primary_theme: multi-agent RL for asymmetric analog circuit placement
